voice.name: Tutorial
voice.description: A learner reads each step while doing it: what to do, what they will see and why it matters for what they are building.
voice.rule: Headlines, headings and claims' statements are 1 to 8 words, sentence case, with no period at the end ("Build a team chat").
A headline states a benefit, a heading its finding, and a sentence before a block what the block shows.
A lede states the page's strongest facts, never a list of what is coming.
A step's prose is passages of two or three sentences, up to 32 words each, varying in length; a one-line instruction stays a short paragraph.
A step says what you do, what you will see and why it matters, joining cause and result in one sentence ("because", "so", "which"), then shows the command and its output.
No metaphors, no adjectives that do not measure something, no hype words, no emoji. Never write "formal verification".
Actions are a verb and an object, 2 to 4 words.
Name SCXML and actor terms exactly (state, event, transition, actor, host). The product name is lowercase: tinyactors.
No serial comma: "states, events and transitions".
Never add a claim, number, name or capability that the page or its sources do not state.
Never name the reader's role ("as a tech lead", "for operators"); write for them by choosing what to explain.
Never explain how the site is made (that a page is generated, captured or checked); say what the thing does for the reader.
The reader is "you". No questions, and no fact that the step's own output does not show.
